State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Mahakali Enterprises vs Ashish Parasar on 21 April, 2016
STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, UTTARAKHAND, DEHRADUN

 FIRST APPEAL NO. 433 / 2010

M/s Mahakali Enterprises
G-3, Surya Complex, Ranipur Mod, Haridwar
 ......Appellant / Opposite Party No. 1

 Versus

1. Sh. Ashish Parashar S/o Sh. Sushil Kumar Parashar
 R/o Mohalla Latowali, Kankhal, Tehsil & District Haridwar
 ......Respondent No. 1 / Complainant

2. Proprietor, Spice Care Center
 B-Electronics Railway Road, Near Mehfil Restaurant
 Jwalapur, Tehsil & District Haridwar
 ......Respondent / Opposite Party No. 2

Mr. Sanjay Yadavi, Learned Counsel for the Appellant
None for Respondent Nos. 1 & 2

Coram: Mr. D.K. Tyagi, H.J.S., Member
 Mrs. Veena Sharma, Member

Dated: 21/04/2016
 ORDER
(Per: Mr. Veena Sharma, Member):
This appeal, under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986,
has been preferred by the appellant-opposite party No. 1 against the order
dated 27.10.2010 passed by the District Forum, Haridwar in consumer
complaint No. 200 of 2009, whereby the District Forum has allowed the
consumer complaint and directed the opposite party No. 1-M/s Mahakali
Enterprises to provide to the complainant a new mobile in place of old one
and if the same is not possible than the opposite party No. 1 pay the cost of
mobile to the complainant and also to pay a damages of Rs. 3,000/- to the
complainant, within one month from the date of order.
2. Briefly stated the facts of the case as mentioned in the consumer
complaint are that the complainant Sh. Ashish Parashar has purchased a
2
mobile phone of Spice company from the opposite party No. 1-Proprietor,
M/s Mahakali Enterprises, Haridwar for a sum of Rs. 6,300/- on 28.07.2008.
Within one month from the date of purchasing the said mobile phone
stopped working. The opposite party No. 2-Spice Care center had given the
complainant another new phone exchanging the old mobile phone. But the
second mobile phone also developed some fault and stopped working and
still not in order. The complainant requested many times to the opposite
parties, but they did not attend his problem. Aggrieving this, the
complainant has filed a consumer complaint before the District Forum,
Haridwar.
3. The opposite party No. 1 has filed written statement before the
District Forum, Haridwar and has pleaded that the consumer complaint filed
by the complainant is baseless and on false ground. The complainant has
filed a bill dated 08.10.2009, but the Sl. No. of the mobile is not readable, so
it is suspected that the complainant has bought the said mobile phone from
answering opposite party. The complainant has not deposited the said
mobile phone in the Forum below. The answering opposite party has not
sold any mobile phone to the complainant. In the bill, which is deposited by
the complainant before the District Forum, it is clearly mentioned "warranty
will be provided by Company's authorized service center only", so if there is
any defect in the mobile phone, then the authorized service center is
responsible to remove the defects in the mobile phone or exchange the same.
The complainant himself stated in his consumer complaint that he had
deposit the said mobile phone to the opposite party No. 2 to remove the
defects in mobile and received back after satisfaction, so no complaint arise.
Therefore, the consumer complaint filed by the complainant is liable to be
dismissed.
4. The opposite party No. 2 has filed written statement before the
District Forum, Haridwar and has pleaded that he was the proprietor/partner
of Spice Care Center. The PCB of the complainant's mobile phone was
totally damaged due to mishandling the mobile. The said mobile was in the
3
guarantee period, so the complainant brought his mobile for repairing in the
service center-answering opposite party. After inspection, the complainant
was informed that the PCB of the said mobile phone is damaged, if we
change the PCB then IMEI number of the said mobile phone will be change.
The complainant gave his consent to change the PCB of the mobile phone.
The answering opposite party has changed the PCB and the said mobile
phone become in perfect condition. After this, complainant never came to
the answering opposite party for any complaint about his mobile phone. The
answering opposite party has not provided the complainant a new mobile
phone, as he was not authorized for the same.
5. The District Forum, on an appreciation of the material on record, has
allowed the consumer complaint vide order dated 27.10.2010 in the above
manner. Aggrieved by the said order, the opposite party No. 1-appellant has
filed this appeal.
6. We have heard Sh. Sanjay Yadav, learned counsel for the appellant
have gone through the entire record of the District Forum and perused the
material placed on record. None appeared on behalf of respondent
Nos. 1 & 2.
7. There is no dispute that the complainant-respondent No. 1 had
purchased a mobile phone of Spice Company modal No. C-810 having IMEI
No. A1000003F38C45 on 28.07.2008 from the opposite party No.1-
appellant for a sum of Rs. 6,300/-. There is also no dispute that after one
month of its purchase, the respondent No. 1 approached to the Spice Care
Center-respondent No. 2, who had changed the said mobile with a new one
with IMEI No. A1000003F38C9E, though the respondent No. 2 has denied
the fact that he provided a new mobile phone in place of old one, rather it
has been mentioned in the written statement of respondent No. 2 that only
PCB board of the mobile phone was replaced. It is to be seen whether the
respondent No. 1 has made Spice Company a necessary party or not, who
4
may be responsible for the change of new mobile in place of old one, which
was said to be out of order after purchase of one month.
8. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the District
Forum has failed to appreciate the fact that the warranty is provided by the
manufacturing company or its service center and not by the shopkeeper. The
respondent No. 1 did not approach to the appellant regarding any
manufacturing defect in the mobile phone and even then the District Forum
has passed order against the appellant-shopkeeper. The District Forum has
failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No. 1 approached to the
service center, who provided a new mobile phone in place of old one,
therefore, there was no responsibility of the appellant-shopkeeper. The
respondent No. 1 has not made manufacturing company of mobile phone as
a necessary party in the consumer complaint before the District Forum. The
appellant has never provided any warranty to the respondent No.1, therefore,
the appellant is not responsible for any manufacturing defect in the mobile
phone. The respondent No. 1 has not proved his complaint by cogent
evidence against the appellant. The respondent No. 1 has not filed any expert
evidence regarding the technical defect in the mobile phone. The District
Forum has passed the impugned order without perused the documents and
evidence filed on the record.
9. Admittedly, the respondent No. 1 had purchased a mobile phone of
Spice Company from the appellant for a sum of Rs. 6,300/- on 28.07.2008.
This mobile phone could not work after a month, therefore, the respondent
No. 1 contacted the respondent No. 2 Spice Care Center, who repaired the
mobile by changing PCB board and handed over to the respondent No. 1.
According to the respondent No. 1 this mobile phone again and again
became defective after a gap of one month or two months, which was
rectified by the respondent No. 2-Spice Care Center, but finally the opposite
parties did not provide services to the respondent No. 1. Therefore, the
consumer complaint was filed. From the perusal of the consumer complaint
it is clear that the respondent No. 1 has not made Spice Company a
5
necessary party in the consumer complaint, who is responsible for the
change of defective piece of mobile with a new mobile phone. The
shopkeeper-appellant is not directly responsible for the change of mobile
phone. By not making Spice Company a necessary party in the consumer
complaint, the consumer complaint is defective due to non-joinder of the
parties. In the affidavit of respondent No. 1 Sh. Yogesh Vadhwa, the
proprietor, has deposed that there is clear cut declaration that "Warranty will
be provided by Company's Authorized Service Center". Therefore, only
Spice Company is responsible for the change of mobile or to return the
money, but the respondent No. 1 has not made Spice Company a necessary
party. The consumer complaint is defective due to non-joinder of the parties.
Appellant is not responsible to provide a new mobile phone in place of old
mobile or to pay any amount to the respondent No. 1, if the new mobile is
not provided.
10. In view of the above discussion, the finding recorded by the District
Forum being perverse and against the evidence on record. The order
impugned passed by the District Forum, Haridwar cannot legally be
sustained and the same is liable to be set aside and, thus, the appeal is fit to
be allowed.
11. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The order impugned dated
27.10.2010 passed by the District Forum, Haridwar is set aside and the
consumer complaint No. 200 of 2009 is dismissed. No order as to costs. The
amount deposited by the appellant as statutory amount at the time of filing
the appeal be released in appellant's favour.
(MRS. VEENA SHARMA) (D.K. TYAGI)
